Order No. 07/ Dated: 03 December, 2025 I.A. No. 14807 of 2025 Heard Mr. Vishnu Prabhakar
Pathak, learned counsel for the appellant and none appears on behalf of the State.
2.  This application has been preferred on behalf of appellant for grant of bail to him, during the pendency of this appeal.

3. The appellant has been convicted for the offence under Section 376(AB) of the IPC and has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for life along with a fine of Rs. 1 Lakh.
4.
It has been alleged that a stranger had committed penetrative assault upon the three years old child of the informant.

Though, submission has been advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant that the identity of the appellant has not been established but it appears that P.W.-1 who happens to be the mother of the victim has categorically stated that the appellant was the person who had taken her daughter in his lap and thereafter, the incident had occurred.
She has also stated that when she had gone to call her brother-in-law, only one person as well as her daughter were present in the house.

sentences.text: The evidence of P.W.-1, therefore, sufficiently indicates about the appellant having committed such act and the evidence of the Doctor who has been examined as P.W.-5 reveals that apart from the abrasion on vaginal wall, there was recent rupture of hymen which is inflamed.
6. On consideration of the aforesaid facts, we are not inclined to admit the appellant on bail.

Accordingly, the prayer for bail of the appellant is hereby rejected.
7.
The aforesaid I.A. stands rejected and disposed of.
